# PREVENTION OF ANTIVIRAL INFECTIONS IN A PATIENT WITH MALIGNANCY

## **Solid Tumors**

## No Antiviral Prophylaxis Recommended

Solid tumors do not significantly compromise the cellular immune system.
Therefore, patients are at low risk for opportunistic viral infections.
Documented invasive viral infections are very rare. Coincidental mucocutaneous infections by herpes simplex are easily treated and do not result in life-threatening invasive infections. Reactivation of Cytomegalovirus (CMV) or Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is rarely observed.

## **Acute Leukemia**

## Herpes simplex virus-seronegative patients

No Antiviral Prophylaxis Recommended
In patients with acute leukemia, treatment is highly aggressive and consists of a combination of various cytotoxic agents administered in sequential cycles as induction, consolidation and maintenance therapy. Persistent, i.e.
10 days and profound neutropenia (<500 neutrophils) regularly occurs and correlates with the risk of developing fever and infections. Almost all viral infections during neutropenia constitute reactivations of herpes viruses.
None of the available studies demonstrated an effect of antiviral prophylaxis on the initiation of antibiotic treatment, number of febrile days, duration of antibiotic treatment, and onset of opportunistic infections. Therefore, no recommendation for antiviral prophylaxis in patients with acute leukemia can be given.

## Herpes simplex virus-seropostive patients

Patients undergoing leukemia induction therapy should receive prophylaxis.
Acyclovir 800 MG PO q12h ($) [R]

## **Lymphoma**

## No Antiviral Prophylaxis Recommended

Rituximab is a monoclonal anti-CD-20 antibody used for treatment of lymphomas. It leads to a profound depletion of circulating B-cells. B-cells recover usually within 3-6 months after treatment. Prolonged administration of rituximab (e.g., maintenance treatment >12 months) may result in a significant decrease of levels of immunoglobulin M. Parvovirus B19 and JC-papovavirus infections have been reported with maintenance rituximab therapy, but drugs that would prevent these infections are not available. There is no substantial increase in risk of reactivation of herpes viruses (including HSV, VZV, and CMV).
Recommend routine testing for Hepatitis B virus prior to initiating Rituximab and other Anti-CD20 antibody therapy in patients.
[Hepatitis B information page](hepatitis-b)
